evidence.title: As US relations fray, Canada gets serious about its own launch industry
evidence.body: [e001:f01] Eric Berger – Oct 1, 2026 11:30 am | 118 The Canada Rocket Company is developing the R-2 rocket. [e001:f02] Credit: Canada Rocket Company The Canada Rocket Company is developing the R-2 rocket. [e001:f03] Credit: Canada Rocket Company Story text Size Width * Links * Subscribers only Learn more A year or two ago, a few Canadian launch companies were trying to develop small rockets, but if we’re being frank, the industry was not particularly notable. [e001:f04] So this spring, the government announced the first awards to three companies—NordSpace, Reaction Dynamics, and Canada Rocket Company—to support work on rockets with “light lift” capability. [e001:f05] Decision to go bigger The initial awards as part of Launch the North were modest, $8.33 million CAD, but the government has signaled larger awards in the future. [e001:f06] Accordingly, one of these three companies, Toronto-based Canada Rocket Company, decided it would skip the small-rocket phase and move directly into a more ambitious medium-launch vehicle. [e001:f07] “The advice we got from having spoken with about 150 engineers, from the director of Starship engineering all the way down to some entry-level folks, is that you’re not going to be able de-risk a rocket development program by building a smaller rocket,” said Hugh Kolias, chief executive of the Canada Rocket Company, in an interview. [e001:f08] There are nine methane-fueled engines, a gas-generator engine cycle, and landing legs that signal a future path toward reuse of the first stage. [e001:f09] If all goes well, Kolias said, the company could be ready to launch by 2032. [e001:f10] Famously, in 1959, the Canadian Prime Minister canceled the Avro Arrow interceptor aircraft under development in the country. [e001:f11] Space is one of the 10 capabilities outlined in the report, which includes “space launch” as a priority. [e001:f12] “We’re pulling a little bit away from the globalist movement and realizing that there are some core aspects, both economically and from a sovereign or defense and military perspective, that you should own your own destiny.” Eventually, Kolias said, the Canadian government might put as much as half a billion dollars on the table for a sovereign launch capability, along with some guarantee of launch contracts. [e001:f13] Canada Rocket Company remains small for now with about 30 people—a core of which are Canadian rocket scientists who left to work at places like SpaceX, Blue Origin, and Rocket Lab but have now returned north. [e001:f14] On Thursday, the company announced that the $30 million Jeremy Hansen Test Facility will be sited on 50 acres leased from the Greater London International Airport Authority and will include an engine test area with up to three vertical and horizontal test stands for static engine testing, capable of testing engines with more than 1MN in thrust (225,000 pounds of thrust). [e001:f15] Perhaps it offers some hope that they can remain good neighbors, with warm relations resuming in the future—while Canada also has the capability to launch its own rockets. [e001:f16] Eric Berger Senior Space Editor Eric Berger Senior Space Editor Eric Berger is the senior space editor at Ars Technica, covering everything from astronomy to private space to NASA policy, and author of two books: Liftoff , about the rise of SpaceX; and Reentry , on the development of the Falcon 9 rocket and Dragon.

evidence.title: Levy: Amid “True Investment Boom” Fed Must Hike to Keep Policy Rate at Neutral
evidence.body: [e005:f01] A visiting fellow at the Hoover Institution and a long-standing member of the Shadow Open Market Committee he is known for his background in economic research, having previously served as Chief Economist at Bank of America and conducted research at the Congressional Budget Office and the American Enterprise Institute. [e005:f02] Mickey says the latest August PCE - personal consumption and ependiture data - “clearly suggests that inflation is sticky and above 3% … And what you’ve seen is … since early 2025 a drift up in core inflation. [e005:f03] And that’s the long ind short of things.” Importantly consumer spending also continued to increase last month. [e005:f04] I mean, basically you can focus on the nuanced comments of the different Fed members, but you can also focus on the bigger picture and the bigger picture of the healthy economic growth, the strong growth in aggregate demand and the high inflation. _That clearly suggests that while the timing may be uncertain around the mid-term elections, the clear message is the Fed’s going to need to raise rates.”_ Mickey views the ongoing wave of business investment—especially in AI, data centers, and modern infrastructure—as one of the defining features of the current U.S. economic landscape. [e005:f05] “_What you have here is a true investment boom_. [e005:f06] But nevertheless, it _’s an investment boom. [e005:f07] And that is associated with high expected rates of return on investment that is naturally associated with higher real interest rates.”_“If this investment boom is pushing up the natural rate, then the Fed has to adjust up its policy rate to reflect that.” Mickey reflects on past waves of technological innovation, such as the 1990’s Dot Com era and the Industrial Revolution. [e005:f08] _“If this investment boom is pushing up the natural rate, then the Fed has to adjust up its policy rate to reflect that._” The implication is clear: as long as the investment-driven expansion continues to lift the natural real rate—the rate consistent with stable inflation and potential growth—the Fed must also shift its policy rate higher just to remain neutral, not merely to tighten policy. [e005:f09] I’d much rather have an environment of higher real interest rates associated with healthy economic performance and an investment boom than low real interest rates associated with disappointing economic performance and weak investment.”_ So dive in and hear why Mickey says the Fed may skip hiking rates before the mid-term elections but after that another rate hike at the end of the year is all but a done deal. [e005:f10] Spoiler alert: he says this is consistent with the FOMC realizing that last year’s three rate cuts in a row right before the end of the year failed to see that policy was not restrictive. ”I think the broad framework for the Fed now is it's probably thinking it has to reverse those rate cuts from last year and raise its policy rate a couple more times back to where it was. [e005:f11] You had an increase of 9/10 of a percent in nominal terms, 6/10 of a percent in real terms for consumption. **Strong consumer, investment and inflation** 00:02:45:08 And so add it all up and you have a resilient economy that is being driven by, you know, a healthy and resilient consumer. [e005:f12] And the boom in business investment spending related to the AI build out. [e005:f13] And then couple that with inflation that’s above 3%. **Rate hikes coming** 00:03:53:02 We’ll see. [e005:f14] That clearly suggests that while the timing may be uncertain around the midterm elections, the clear message is the Fed’s going to need to raise rates. **Surprising growth** 00:05:44:12 I don’t know if it’s stronger than people thought, but when you add up all of the economic data that you’ve just presented, it shows a healthy economy, meaning it’s growing faster. [e005:f15] Labor markets have bounced back from the temporary weakness of last year, where employment was flat for, you know, a handful of months. **In a word, STRONG** 00:06:22:19 And, you know, all the signals are business investment is strong not just for AI but for basic investment in machinery and the like. [e005:f16] That may be a little more accentuated now, because not only you can’t only look at the current 3% rate of inflation, but the cumulative impact since just before the Covid pandemic, you know, the consumer prices are up about 30%. **The uneven burden of inflation** 00:09:30:07 And that weighs very heavily and is having。

evidence.title: Nasdaq Calypso Launches Agentic Capabilities
evidence.body: [e007:f01] At its core, Nasdaq has established an agentic AI operating environment within its Nasdaq Calypso platform, providing financial institutions with a contained, governed space to run, connect, and scale AI agents across the trade lifecycle. [e007:f02] “For institutions to adopt AI agents at scale, they need a trusted, governed infrastructure inside the capital market platforms they already run, a place to connect agents from many different sources to real workflows, data, and controls,” said Magnus Haglind, Head of Capital Markets Technology at Nasdaq. [e007:f03] “By integrating agentic capabilities and serving as the orchestration layer, we are evolving Nasdaq Calypso from a system of record into an intelligent platform that automates activity at every stage of the trade lifecycle.” AI has enormous potential across capital market workflows to enhance risk controls, reduce settlement failures, and transform operational data into automated actions. [e007:f04] According to a recent Nasdaq and Acuiti survey , almost half of respondents highlighted challenges relating to manual intervention within their post-trade operations, while 56% said they risk losing ground to competitors if they do not integrate AI or machine learning into their clearing operations. [e007:f05] How the Nasdaq Calypso Agentic AI Environment Will Work Nasdaq Calypso is an advanced capital markets and treasury platform used by banks, brokers, asset managers, central banks, and other financial institutions to process front-to-back office trading, risk management, and collateral workflows. [e007:f06] The operating environment will allow clients to access Nasdaq Calypso’s agents and connect their own proprietary AI infrastructure through an integrated layer built on the Model Context Protocol (MCP). [e007:f07] It will enable agents to operate on core Nasdaq Calypso data, drawing on the platform’s system-of-record trading, risk, and collateral records, and can be extended with additional enterprise, market, and reference data sources. [e007:f08] The launch also aligns with the first agentic capabilities available in the environment: a natural language assistant that lets users query the platform’s data, documentation, and other information. [e007:f09] Nasdaq plans to roll out a suite of governed agentic workers designed to address operational friction caused by manual processes that persist across capital market workflows. [e007:f10] The agents will be hosted by Nasdaq and delivered through Nasdaq Calypso’s cloud environment, which is built on Amazon Bedrock to provide the scalable services and governance controls required to run agentic AI in regulated environments. [e007:f11] Nasdaq will partner with individual clients as they work through internal AI governance and control requirements to bring these capabilities online. [e007:f12] The launch builds on Nasdaq’s extensive AI capabilities within its suite of Financial Technology platforms, including Nasdaq Verafin’s Agentic AI workforce leveraged by 800+ clients, and AI-powered regulatory reporting in Nasdaq AxiomSL.
